start-here: start here guide onboarding stage-0 start here (stage 0 kickoff for jacob) start here (stage 0 kickoff for jacob) you know the english nt well and think in engineering terms. good — greek here rewards that: pattern recognition over memorization, reading over flashcards. this page is the concrete on ramp; learning path has the full curriculum. everything below is free. (a) decide once: pronunciation see pronunciation erasmian vs restored koine (https://danielstreett.com/2011/12/01/the great greek pronunciation debate sbl 2011 report pt 3/) for the full neutral overview. short version: erasmian — 16th c. reconstruction, historically inaccurate but it's what nearly every seminary, textbook, and free video course uses. restored koine — linguistically closer to how 1st century speakers actually sounded (majority view among historical phonologists), used by immersion programs like biblical language center living koine greek. neither affects grammar or comprehension — it's purely how you voice the letters. trade off: restored koine is the historically "truer" sound; erasmian is the practically compatible one. default: erasmian , because daily dose of greek and biblicaltraining mounce nt201 (your weeks 1–2 tools below) both use it. switching later costs you a few weeks of re hearing sounds, not months — it is cheap to change once you have reasons to. (b) set up (30 min) [ ] step bible — interlinear/morphology/lexicon platform. https://www.stepbible.org/ — bookmark it now, you'll use it in week 2. [ ] logeion — free multi dictionary greek lexicon (univ. of chicago). https://logeion.uchicago.edu/ — bookmark for later stages. [ ] daily dose of greek — daily verse videos (rob plummer, phd). site: https://dailydoseofgreek.com/ — subscribe by entering your name/email on the homepage (5 weekly 2 min videos), or use the free ios/android app for daily notifications + full archive. [ ] biblicaltraining mounce nt201 — free 36 lecture video course. https://www.biblicaltraining.org/learn/institute/nt201 biblical greek — create a free account to track progress. [ ] billmounce site — mounce's own free lecture/vocab hub. https://www.billmounce.com/ [ ] bible hub interlinear (t3, quick fallback only — verify anything load bearing against step or a lexicon; see step bible): https://biblehub.com/interlinear/1 john/1 1.htm [ ] free greek text online — pick one to skim now, you'll read it for real in stage 2: tc sblgnt https://sblgnt.com/ (download page; documented eclectic text) or tc tyndale house greek new testament https://thegreeknewtestament.com/ (fresh independent edition, sample of mark free online). (c) weeks 1–2, day by day (10–25 min/day) 1. day 1 (20 min): alphabet chunk 1 — α β γ δ ε ζ η θ (names + sounds, erasmian). use mounce basics of biblical greek ch. 1 or greek alphabet and diacritics as your reference table. 2. day 2 (20 min): alphabet chunk 2 — ι κ λ μ ν ξ ο π. say each aloud. 3. day 3 (20 min): alphabet chunk 3 — ρ σ/ς τ υ φ χ ψ ω. full alphabet review, uppercase + lowercase + final sigma. 4. day 4 (15 min): breathings (smooth/rough) and the iota subscript — see greek alphabet and diacritics. practice on 5 real nt words. 5. day 5 (15 min): the three accents (acute/grave/circumflex) — what they mark, why you can mostly ignore them for now (pitch, not stress, in the historical system). read greek alphabet and diacritics. 6. day 6 (15 min): read the whole alphabet aloud, uppercase and lowercase, from memory. time yourself; repeat until under 60 seconds. 7. day 7 (10 min): first daily dose of greek video — pick any verse from the archive, just get the habit started. (https://dailydoseofgreek.com/) 8. day 8 (25 min): biblicaltraining mounce nt201 lecture 1 — "the greek language" (alphabet, pronunciation, grammar overview). 9. day 9 (25 min): nt201 lecture 3 — "the alphabet and pronunciation" (gamma nasals, vowels, diphthongs, breathing marks in more depth). 10. day 10 (20 min): transcribe 1 john 1:1 letter by letter by hand from a printed/screen greek text (e.g. via step bible or tc sblgnt) — slow, deliberate, no typing. 11. day 11 (20 min): second daily dose of greek video; note any letters/sounds still shaky and drill those specifically. 12. day 12 (25 min): open step bible (https://www.stepbible.org/) and hover parse every word of 1 john 1:1–4 — just look, don't try to memorize the grammar terms yet. 13. day 13 (15 min): nt201 lecture 4 — "punctuation and syllabification." re read your day 10 transcription and check it against the syllable rules. 14. day 14 (15 min): read 1 john 1:1–4 aloud, erasmian pronunciation, from the text you transcribed. don't worry about comprehension — this is decoding fluency. this is the same passage 1 john 1 1 4 first reading walks through in more depth. (d) then move to stage 1 in learning path once you can write all 24 letters + diacritics from memory and have step bible + logeion bookmarked. for a guided first real reading, see 1 john 1 1 4 first reading.
